instagram.title: Symmetry and the snowflake
instagram.caption:
Symmetry and the snowflake

Six arms, six mirrors. The shape of a water molecule decides the shape of a snowflake.

Turn a starfish by a fifth of a circle and it looks the same. Fold a butterfly down the middle and the halves match. Those are the two basic kinds of symmetry: turning and mirroring.

The six arms do not talk to each other. The arms of a snowflake match, so it seems they must coordinate. They do not.

Try the free interactive lesson on kaizen-cosmos.pages.dev (link in bio). No sign-up.
